def: An MHC class II allele associated with rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes.
Antibody deficiency with low IgG and IgA and recurrent sinopulmonary infections, usually presenting in adulthood from defective B-cell differentiation. Raises risk of autoimmunity and lymphoma.
Plasma separated from donated blood and frozen soon after collection. Contains all clotting factors; used to correct coagulopathy such as warfarin reversal or DIC.
Ratio of ankle to arm systolic blood pressure. Values below 0.9 indicate peripheral artery disease.
IV fluid containing 5% dextrose in water. It supplies free water once the glucose is metabolized and so lowers serum sodium.
The CDC advisory group that sets US vaccine recommendations.
Membrane proteins that mediate fusion of vesicles with target membranes, as in neurotransmitter release. Cleaved by botulinum and tetanus toxins.
Nucleotide that G proteins bind in their inactive state; exchange for GTP activates them.
Peptide hormone from ACE action on angiotensin I. Constricts arterioles, stimulates aldosterone and ADH release and raises blood pressure.
Synthetic estrogen given in pregnancy in the past. Exposed daughters develop clear cell adenocarcinoma of the vagina and structural uterine anomalies.
Sexually transmitted infection by Chlamydia trachomatis serotypes L1-L3, causing painless ulcer then tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (buboes).
Proliferation of atypical cells in breast lobules that doesn't invade. A marker of increased risk of invasive cancer in either breast; E-cadherin is lost.
Fast heart rhythm (3 or more beats above 100/min) arising in the ventricles, with wide QRS complexes. Can degenerate to ventricular fibrillation.
Percentage of the end-diastolic volume of the left ventricle ejected with each beat. Normal is about 55 to 70%.
Oxygen pressure in the alveolar gas, calculated by the alveolar gas equation. Used to find the A-a gradient.
Hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus in the airways of patients with asthma or cystic fibrosis. Causes wheezing, mucus plugging and central bronchiectasis with high IgE.
A proto-oncogene encoding a small GTPase in the RAS pathway. Activating mutations occur in colorectal, pancreatic and lung cancers and predict lack of response to EGFR antibodies.
Anemia from red cells shredded by passing through small vessels with fibrin strands or clots. Smear shows schistocytes; seen in TTP, HUS and DIC.
Defect in fatty acid oxidation causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia, vomiting and lethargy during fasting.
Purine nucleotide that is the branch point to AMP and GMP in de novo purine synthesis.
Measure of transferrin capacity to bind iron. High in iron deficiency and low in anemia of chronic disease.
Brainstem gaze center for horizontal eye movements toward the same side. Lesions cause ipsilateral gaze palsy.
Staph aureus strain susceptible to methicillin-type penicillins like nafcillin and oxacillin.
Life-threatening reaction to antipsychotics with fever, muscle rigidity, altered mental status and autonomic instability. Treat with dantrolene.
Antigen-recognition complex on T cells, binding peptide presented on MHC molecules.
T-cell surface protein binding CD40 on B cells to enable isotype switching. Absent in hyper-IgM syndrome.
Crystal that deposits in joints in gout. Appears needle-shaped and negatively birefringent.
Pressure in the vena cava near the right atrium, reflecting volume status and right heart function.
Anterior knee pain from the patella tracking poorly over the femur, common in young athletes and runners.
Thyroid hormone precursor made by iodination of monoiodotyrosine; two DIT molecules form T4.
Transcription factor in the thymus that displays self-antigens for negative selection. Mutation causes APECED.
Receptor tyrosine kinase overexpressed in some breast and gastric cancers. Targeted by trastuzumab.
Tumor suppressor gene for DNA repair; mutations raise risk of breast, ovarian, prostate and pancreatic cancers.
Heart rate of the fetus, normally 110 to 160 beats per minute.
Intermediate filament marker of astrocytes, used to identify glial tumors.
Volume of blood in a ventricle at the end of filling; a measure of preload.
Family of growth factors for cell proliferation and angiogenesis. FGFR3 mutations cause achondroplasia.
Cyanotic congenital heart defect with VSD, pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta and right ventricular hypertrophy.
Lipoprotein remnant formed as VLDL loses triglycerides; converted to LDL.
Percentage of hemoglobin saturated with oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry.
Protease that cleaves von Willebrand factor multimers. Deficiency causes thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
AML subtype with t(15;17) PML-RARA, Auer rods and DIC; treated with all-trans retinoic acid.
Electron carrier produced in the citric acid cycle and beta-oxidation that donates electrons to complex II.
Alkalinizing agent used to treat metabolic acidosis or tricyclic overdose.
Kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplant.
Antidepressants that block monoamine oxidase. Risk hypertensive crisis with tyramine and serotonin syndrome.
B-cell surface marker in all stages of B-cell development.
Impaired adduction of one eye on lateral gaze from a medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion; classic in multiple sclerosis.
Cells such as dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells that display antigen on MHC to T cells.
Illness caused by SARS-CoV-2.
Disorder from NF2 gene mutation causing bilateral vestibular schwannomas and meningiomas.
Childhood disorder with severe recurrent temper outbursts and persistent irritability.
Nontreponemal screening test for syphilis that detects antibodies against cardiolipin.
Bacterial enzymes for cell wall synthesis that beta-lactams bind. Altered in MRSA.
Amphetamine derivative (ecstasy) that releases serotonin; causes hyperthermia and hyponatremia.
Fat accumulation in the liver unrelated to alcohol, linked to obesity and insulin resistance.
Imaging technique that measures bone mineral density to diagnose osteoporosis.
Chemokine receptor; HIV uses it for entry into T cells.
Surgery to realign a fracture and fix it with plates or screws.
HIV drugs binding reverse transcriptase directly, e.g., efavirenz.
Test measuring thyroid uptake of radioiodine; high in Graves and low in thyroiditis.
Chronic arthritis beginning before age 16 without another cause.
Anti-D antibody given to Rh-negative mothers to prevent sensitization to fetal Rh-positive cells.
Coronavirus respiratory illness first seen in 2002.
Adrenal androgen; high levels suggest adrenal source of androgen excess.
Neutrophils with multilobed nuclei, first responders in acute inflammation.
Menstrual bleeding outside normal frequency, duration or volume.
Gut hormone from K cells that boosts insulin release after meals.
Long, unbranched polysaccharides of repeating disaccharides; components of proteoglycans.
Drugs with tissue-specific estrogen agonist or antagonist action, such as tamoxifen and raloxifene.
BRCA1 and BRCA2 DNA-repair tumor suppressors; mutation raises breast and ovarian cancer risk.
Growth factor that stimulates epithelial cell proliferation via its receptor EGFR.
Homeobox genes that specify body segment identity along the head-to-tail axis.
Delayed conduction in the right bundle, with rSR' (rabbit ears) in V1 and wide QRS.
Neutrophil serine protease; the target of c-ANCA in granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Fast regular rhythm arising above the ventricles, with a narrow QRS.
Risk score for stroke in atrial fibrillation, used to decide anticoagulation.
Infection of the heart valves or endocardium, causing fever, murmur and vegetations.
Atrial fibrillation or flutter with fast conduction to the ventricles, with heart rate above 100.
Inherited thickening of the left ventricle, usually from sarcomere gene mutations, causing diastolic dysfunction and sudden cardiac death in young athletes.

term: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
def: Systolic heart failure with ejection fraction of 40% or below.
Persistent opening between the atria that can allow paradoxical embolism.
Cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase and for tyrosine and tryptophan hydroxylase; deficiency can cause phenylketonuria-like disease.
Drugs such as losartan that block the AT1 receptor; no cough, unlike ACE inhibitors.
Enzyme on HDL that esterifies cholesterol; deficiency causes corneal clouding.
Fats made of three fatty acids on a glycerol backbone; the main storage lipid.
Progressive scarring of the lung of unknown cause, with a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern.
cAMP-dependent kinase that phosphorylates target proteins.
Clot in a deep vein, usually of the leg; risk of pulmonary embolism.
Childhood disease with large cystic kidneys and congenital hepatic fibrosis.
Inherited kidney fibrosis with slowly progressive renal failure and bland urine sediment.
Wilms tumor, aniridia, genitourinary anomalies and intellectual disability from deletion of 11p13.
Tumor suppressor gene on 11p13 associated with Wilms tumor.
Enzyme that degrades catecholamines and levodopa. Inhibited by entacapone.
Gene mutated in hereditary hemochromatosis (C282Y), causing iron overload.
Transporter loading monoamines into synaptic vesicles; blocked by reserpine and tetrabenazine.
Measure of variation in red blood cell size; raised in iron deficiency.
Aggressive malignancy of T cells from HTLV-1 infection, with hypercalcemia.
Retrovirus that causes adult T-cell leukemia and tropical spastic paraparesis.
Limited systemic sclerosis with Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly and Telangiectasias; anticentromere antibodies.
Region of the abdomen containing stomach, spleen and left kidney.
Porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency causing abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric symptoms and dark urine.
Oxygen saturation of blood in the pulmonary artery, showing oxygen extraction.
Thin-slice chest CT showing detailed lung parenchyma, used in interstitial lung disease.
Functional classes I-IV of heart failure based on symptoms with activity.
Iodine-131 given to ablate thyroid tissue in hyperthyroidism or thyroid cancer.
Pneumococcal vaccine covering 23 serotypes, for adults and high-risk patients.
Conjugate vaccine covering 15 pneumococcal serotypes.
Blood test for latent tuberculosis detecting T-cell interferon-gamma release.
Tick-borne Rickettsia rickettsii infection with fever, headache and a rash starting on wrists and ankles.
Plain abdominal radiograph used to look for stones and obstruction.

term: Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network
def: Group that created head trauma decision rules for children.
Coxsackievirus illness with oral ulcers and vesicles on the hands and feet.
Severe respiratory illness caused by a coronavirus spread from camels.
Antibody preparation given after exposure to chickenpox to high-risk patients.
Catheter that measures uterine contraction strength during labor.
Fatty liver with inflammation and hepatocyte injury, which can lead to cirrhosis.
Backward flow of urine from the bladder into the ureters, predisposing to pyelonephritis.
Severe mucocutaneous drug reaction with skin detachment under 10% body surface and mucosal erosions.
Hypothalamic hormone stimulating GH release from the pituitary.
Calcium-sensing receptor inactivating mutation causing mild hypercalcemia with low urinary calcium.
Synthetic ADH analog used for central diabetes insipidus and bleeding disorders.
IgG subclass raised in IgG4-related disease, which causes fibrosing inflammation of organs.
Liver protein binding testosterone and estradiol in blood.
Cyclin-dependent kinase 4 driving the G1 to S transition; mutations are associated with familial melanoma.
Unequal blood flow between monochorionic twins through placental vascular connections.
DNA repair joining broken double-strand ends without a template; defective in ataxia-telangiectasia and similar.
Accessory pathway causing pre-excitation with a delta wave and risk of tachyarrhythmias.
Pressure in the left ventricle at end of filling, reflecting preload.
Holes in the septum between the ventricles; the most common congenital heart defect.
Thickening of the left ventricular wall from pressure overload such as hypertension.
Thiazide diuretic blocking NCC in the distal tubule; causes hypokalemia and hypercalcemia.
Protein that promotes LDL receptor degradation; inhibitors lower LDL cholesterol.
